BEFORE THE PUBLIC SERVICE COMMISSION
                                 OF THE STATE OF MISSOURI

In the Matter of Evergy Metro, Inc. d/b/a                          )
Evergy Missouri Metro’s Request for                                )      Case No. ER-2026-0143
Authority to Implement a General Rate                              )
Increase for Electric Service                                      )

        EVERGY MISSOURI METRO’S REPLY IN FURTHER SUPPORT OF ITS
       MOTION TO STRIKE PORTIONS OF THE SURREBUTTAL TESTIMONIES
    OF PUBLIC COUNSEL WITNESSES DAVID C. SHAPLEY AND PAUL J. ALVAREZ

           COMES NOW, Evergy Metro, Inc. d/b/a Evergy Missouri Metro (“EMM” or the

“Company”) replies to Public Counsel’s Response in Opposition to Evergy Missouri Metro’s

Motion, filed September 29, 2026 (the “Response”), and states as follows:

           1.       The Response leaves two key points undisputed. It does not contend that Section

VI of either OPC surrebuttal responds to anything in the Company’s rebuttal testimony, and thus

OPC concedes that its testimony is not proper surrebuttal. Nor does OPC oppose the Company’s

alternative request for leave to file the sur-surrebuttal testimony of Messrs. Rietcheck and Reuter

tendered with the Motion. At a minimum, the Commission should therefore grant such leave.

           2.       Public Counsel’s defense of Section VI is merely a flawed account of the parties’

discovery. 1 The Commission need not resolve the flaws in that account, because it does not change

the appropriate result. However the data request timing is explained, Public Counsel presented

$87.8 million in new transmission disallowances, together with a recommendation to amend the

Company’s large load tariffs, in the last round of pre-filed testimony. 2 The Company has had no

opportunity to answer any of it in writing.




1
    See Response ¶¶ 7–22.
2
    Shapley Surrebuttal at pp. 27–33; Alvarez Surrebuttal at pp. 28–32.

                                                           1
         3.       The Commission’s rules supply the procedure for this situation. No party may

supplement its pre-filed testimony without leave. 3 Mr. Shapley recognizes as much, as he reserves

the right to add to his testimony “as necessary and appropriate, and as the Commission permits.”4

Public Counsel sought no leave before presenting Section VI. By contrast, the Company did seek

leave to file its proposed responses, which it tendered with the Motion. 5 The Commission should

strike Section VI, or at least grant the Company’s request for leave.

        4.       The Company is entitled to answer a challenge to the prudence of its investment. A

utility’s expenditures are presumed prudent, but the presumption yields once another party raises

serious doubt, and the utility then bears the burden of dispelling that doubt. 6 That sequence, of

course, assumes the utility has a chance to respond. The order of pre-filed testimony secures that

chance by giving each witness “the last word on their own evidence,” 7 and Section 536.070(2)

guarantees each party the right “to rebut the evidence against him or her.” 8 But because Section

VI arrived in surrebuttal, the Company has had neither the last word nor the opportunity to rebut.

        5.       Public Counsel argues without support that the Company has shown no harm. 9 Not

so, as the harm is what the record would lack if the proposed testimony of Messrs. Rietcheck and

Reuter is not admitted. Mr. Rietcheck’s proposed testimony explains why the four transmission

projects Mr. Shapley challenges were prudent when the decisions were made, and it corrects the

factual premises of his line-rebuild adjustments, including the age of the poles, the number of

structures replaced, and the net book value of the retired plant. 10 Mr. Reuter’s proposed testimony

  Motion ¶ 15 & Attachments 1–2.

  Order Granting Motion to Strike, p. 3, In re: KCP&L Greater Missouri Operations Co., No. ER-2016-0156 (July 26,
2016).
8
  Section 536.070(2), RSMo.
9
  Response, WHEREFORE clause.
10
   See Motion, Attachment 1 at pp. 3–19.

                                                       2
 shows that Panasonic reimbursed the actual cost of the distribution facilities that serve it, and that

the transmission facilities Mr. Alvarez targets are regional Southwest Power Pool upgrades whose

revenue requirement is spread among all transmission customers in the region, with EMM

responsible for a load-ratio share of about 6.86 percent. 11 Without that testimony, the Commission

would decide $87.8 million in disallowances on a written record that contains only Public

Counsel’s opinions in improper surrebuttal, and the Company would be penalized for the timing

of Public Counsel’s own testimony and procedural improprieties.

           6.       The proposed sur-surrebuttal testimony has been on file since September 23 and is

limited to the Section VI material. Public Counsel may cross-examine both witnesses at the

hearing that begins October 5. It is also the relief the Commission granted in the 2016 proceeding

the Motion describes. 12 The Response does not suggest otherwise, and so OPC has conceded that

there is no harm to it if the Commission grants leave.

           WHEREFORE, Evergy Metro, Inc. d/b/a Evergy Missouri Metro respectfully requests

that the Commission grant the relief requested in the Motion, including striking the subject

testimony or, at a minimum, leave to file the sur-surrebuttal testimony of Messrs. Rietcheck and

Reuter attached to the Motion as Attachments 1 and 2; that it rule before the evidentiary hearing

begins on October 5, 2026; and that it grant such other and further relief as the Commission deems

just and reasonable.
